records.name: Calais, Guînes, Hames; English Crown fortified Pale
records.authority: Henry VIII of England via royal governor/garrison
records.summary: Continued English-administered town/fortified jurisdiction. Calais/Guînes English fortification archaeology; 1525 commission & 1529 settlement laws reveal disputed countryside; no precise Tudor survey-derived polygon.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Guînes militarized frontier agricultural tenant district
records.authority: Henry VIII Guînes commission and later ordinances
records.summary: 1525 Crown commission investigated English settler colonization and security; 1529 laws sought to move English arable farmers in, expel foreign tenant farmers, restrict mixed marriages and compel English language. Important legal state action; actual demographic execution is separate evidence.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Ardres, French fortified town near Guînes
records.summary: 1520 Field of Cloth of Gold on neutral ground between English Guînes and French Ardres; France retains Ardres as separate town.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Northern France/Brittany invaded and raided 1522–1523
records.authority: Thomas Howard Earl of Surrey and Charles Brandon Duke of Suffolk, with allies
records.summary: Destructive English operations in France and Scotland attacked rural populations and towns; no scholarly evidence for stable new Tudor-run province from these campaigns.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Irish English Pale under Thomas Howard earl of Surrey
records.authority: Henry VIII-appointed lieutenant Surrey, separate local borough, Pale lords and Irish chiefs
records.summary: Surrey appointed 10 Mar1520, physically governs Pale 1520–March1522. Crown soldiers supplemented forces and made frontier raids; royal programme for wholesale extension of common law/land revenue failed. Not whole-island control.
records.spatial_method: dashed_prior_1488_legal_Pale_line_approx; city sites known, don't paint 4 modern shires
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Monasteroris Castle, O'Connor Faly lordship
records.authority: Surrey's force left ward in captured O'Connor castle
records.summary: 1521 July Deputy Surrey besieged castle with ordnance, took and garrisoned, time to evacuation unknown. This does not make all Offaly royal administered.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Irish deputy Piers Butler Ormond/Ossory
records.authority: Piers Butler, successor to Surrey as deputy
records.summary: From March1522 Ormond office/militia replaced expensive Surrey retinue; Kildare restored to deputy in 1524. Local authority remained contested with Gaelic chiefs and Earl Kildare.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Restored Kildare deputy rule 1524–26
records.authority: Gerald ninth Earl of Kildare under Henry VIII
records.summary: Kildare regained deputy position in 1524 but recalled 1526 amid factional and political dispute; continued authority of local Gaelic dynasties across Ireland.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Lord Delvin Lord Deputy 1527–1528
records.authority: Richard Nugent Baron Delvin under Henry VIII
records.summary: Henry attempted cheap defensive governance through border baron; in May1528 O'Connor Faly captured the deputy; effective power of Dublin crown administrators severely weakened.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Offaly Uí Failghe/ O'Connor lordship
records.authority: Brian O'Connor Faly and factional local competitors
records.summary: Brian O'Connor raided Pale, held royal deputy Delvin May 1528 until Jan1529; royal grant/royal supremacy claims did not translate into territorial governance.
records.note: A single military capture or royal acknowledgement does not transfer a whole province; some periods are documented only as discrete events.

records.name: Ossory/Piers Butler crown deputy 1528–29
records.authority: Piers Ruadh Butler, Earl of Ossory
records.summary: Appointed deputy 4 Aug1528, investiture Oct; 1529–30 replaced with commission; territorial efficacy in Pale is subject of conflict between local nobles.

records.name: Kingdom of Scotland (James V)
records.authority: James V Scottish Crown, Albany regency, Angus control until 1528
records.summary: Remained independent Kingdom of Scotland. English attacks 1522–24 and 1523 border burns did not mean English annexation. King escaped Angus in 1528 and exercised own power.

records.authority: John Rut expedition sponsored by Henry VIII
records.summary: Mary Guildford visited Newfoundland/Labrador in 1527, no Royal administrative land title or English permanent settlement demonstrated. Samson separated, fate uncertain.
